reviewer: Claude simulated category judge, round two, independent scoring

reasons: A1: The paper itself says a matched quality comparison is absent. A09 shows evaluation/training overlap (73 of 186) and no model comparison was run. There is no measured quality improvement, so the score cannot exceed 1.

A2: The prototype impact analyser, QLoRA design and control workspace are documented concepts. The deployed model is unproven and A01-A07 illustrate interfaces only. The originality is credible as a design but unproven in operation.

A3: Two quarters of reported use, reusable prompts and version-controlled controls suggest adaptability. A08 (59 synthetic utility tests) is a narrow technical check. No longitudinal or maintained-quality record exists.

A4: 257 person-days net of review is a single team-reported assertion (S01 digest) with no ledger or approval record. The 8-to-4-hour task is nested inside that total. The 'quality maintained' half of the criterion is unevidenced.

A5: No satisfaction, adoption or stakeholder-outcome measure exists. The one bounded task example is one person's time. The 85% coverage figure has no numerator, denominator or period and is correctly disclaimed.
editorial_fixes: Delete or attribute to a named source these figures: 'approximately 25 regular participants', 'grew from 50 to 60 associates', and 'seven configurable AI controls and ten versioned prompt templates'. None appears in the S01 digest or the exhibit index. If they cannot be sourced, remove them.

Harmonise review-time wording. Section 3 says review time was 'deducted'; section 4 says it is 'included in the calculation'. Use one phrasing: 'Review time was deducted in the reported figure (S01); the calculation has not been inspected.'

In section 2, the sentence 'Exhibits A03 and A04 illustrate local interfaces' sits inside the accessibility-model paragraph. The index says A03 is a platform introduction and A04 a knowledge interface. Reword to 'A03 and A04 show a platform introduction and a knowledge interface; they do not show accessibility analysis or model identity.'
Add after the A01/A02 sentence: 'A01 figures are local evaluation data, not client results.'
Retitle section 5 to 'Outcomes for assurance teams'. Remove or qualify the 'service users' paragraph, since no service-user evidence exists. State it as design intent only.
Keep 'reported' as written. Do not convert it to 'estimated' and do not state that an export is being compiled.
missing_evidence: Packageable now: the S01 digest as source attribution only; A08 and A09 as scoped technical and adverse-integrity artefacts; A01-A07 as illustrations.
Absent: Pulse export or task ledger, review-time deductions, approval record from Delivery Excellence and the delivery lead.
Absent: any matched before/after quality measure, such as defect escape, review rejection rate or test-case acceptance.
Absent: definition, numerator, denominator and period for the 85% figure.
Absent: proof of the deployed model, or an independent holdout with a frozen candidate set and a two-model comparison.
Absent: any stakeholder satisfaction or outcome record.

reasons: N1: N01 shows 7,532 requests against a 7,200 target (about 104.6%), but both displayed P90 values breach the 4,000 ms SLA with four samples each. This shows failure detection, not requirements met or exceeded.

N2: A production-traffic query approach and profile design are described. Only volume is evidenced. Transaction mix, environment comparability and sample adequacy are not, and the 125% production label is unresolved.
N3: Three releases are reported with no dates, acceptance records or observation window. The over-90% effort claims have no baseline hours (N03). Release confidence is asserted, not demonstrated.

N4: Goals, tooling and resources are clearly described. Results are mostly narrative. The 285 passing tests concern the analysis tooling, not client scenarios. The dashboard snapshot has no evidence ID in the pack.

N5: This is the strongest criterion. It offers a candid account of the cache reproduction method, the 7-of-64 telemetry coverage gap and the data-rebuild constraints. The score is capped because there are no paired before/after numbers or retest records (N02, N04).
editorial_fixes: Add source attribution or soften these statements, which are absent from the N02-N04 digests: 'previously appeared successful' runs, 'distinguish idle resources from collection errors', 'unrecoverable after roughly 24 hours', six sources / four formats / ten rules, 16 data files, and the dashboard snapshot (11 projects, 10 bugs). Either cite a digest locator or reword as 'the delivery narrative reports'.

Several first-person statements read as verified fact: 'We also corrected failure paths', 'Routine repopulation is automated', and 'The framework has been applied to AKS migration programmes'. Prefix with 'The delivery narrative reports' as in neighbouring passages.

In the summary, change 'Existing evidence shows achieved workload volumes' to 'A transcribed workload visual reports achieved volume against target'. This keeps the digest from being read as independent verification.
State plainly in the N01 paragraph that the 104.6% figure is calculated from transcribed values and is the only volume ratio used.
Do not state three releases had 'no issues'. The paper already omits this and should continue to.
missing_evidence: Packageable now: N01 transcription with image fingerprints, the N02-N04 digests with locators, and the arithmetic (7,532/7,200; 7/64).
Absent: original unredacted visuals in a form that can be shared. They must stay withheld until redacted.
Absent: any passing acceptance run, or a retest after the failed P90 alert.
Absent: baseline and post-automation hours, run counts and period for the over-90% claims.
Absent: a numeric before/after cache measurement with matched workload, change ID and acceptance.
Absent: gate-retest output for telemetry coverage and raw test logs for the 285 tests.
Absent: release dates, acceptance records, an observation window and a production-volume baseline for the 50x claim.

reasons: I1: Tag-based contribution with shared execution is a sensible ownership model. The paper honestly calls it an application of existing technology. No comparison with prior practice or measured benefit exists.

I2: The driver (the central team cannot hold every domain) and the design (three pipelines, template utility) are clear. The pack contains no code, pipeline history or run records, so implementation is unverified.
I3: A boundary-pushing attempt is conceivable but not substantiated. The paper itself says wider adoption and comparative impact are not established. Nothing evidences a comparative contribution.
I4: Five teams are reported and the delivered assets are listed. No result, benefit or coverage measure exists, and setup-timing claims are explicitly withheld because they conflict.
I5: The maintenance obligation, triage routing and the timing-scope conflict are candidly evaluated. There is no completed contribute-fail-triage-fix-rerun example to show the response working.
editorial_fixes: The summary and section 1 say 'five teams onboarded' and 'five service teams onboarded'. The S02 digest says only that five service teams are on a shared platform. Reword to 'the source describes five service teams on the shared platform' and drop 'onboarded' unless a primary record shows it.
Section 1 states that one maintained scenario 'reduces the need to author a second platform copy'. This is design intent, not an observed benefit. Reword to 'is intended to reduce'.

Attribute or soften statements not in the S02 digest: structured results and traces published after failed runs, and dependency installation and browser provisioning. Use 'the source describes' or delete.
Keep the sentence that adoption is not established. Do not add any statement about external adopters, in either direction.
In section 5, change 'ready to be evaluated through its team and run records' to a plain statement that those records are not yet in the evidence pack.
missing_evidence: Packageable now: the S02 digest with locator, and the design description (tag convention, three pipelines, template utility) as reported design.
Absent: repository or pipeline history showing contributions and shared-run records per team.
Absent: a completed triage example from failure through owner assignment, fix and green rerun.
Absent: a matched setup-timing comparison with consistent task scope.
Absent: any measured regression benefit, such as duplicate-maintenance reduction or coverage change, and any comparison with prior practice that would support I3.

council_recommendation: A 4/5 on every criterion is not defensible for any paper. Round two shows a plateau caused by absent primary evidence, not by writing quality. The revisions have usefully removed several unsupported claims, and the digests add traceability but not proof. Remaining editorial work is small and needs no new facts. For AI, delete or source the unattributed team-size, participant and control/template figures, harmonise the review-time wording, and drop the service-user claims. For NFT, attribute or soften the statements missing from the digests and change first-person assertions to 'the narrative reports'. For Innovation, replace 'onboarded' with the digest's wording and mark benefits as intended. Cross-paper scope is now cleaner: the AI paper owns account savings and the specialist applications, the NFT paper owns PerfOps and Perf Insights, and Innovation owns only shared regression. Keep that boundary and keep unrelated programme figures out. Scores will only move with evidence acquisition: the Pulse ledger and approval record, a matched quality comparison, an independent holdout, a passing NFT run and retest, before/after cache data, release records, and shared-regression run history with a completed triage example. Until those exist, expect roughly 8 to 9 out of 25 per paper.
